quickfire.question: When inserting into a BST, a value smaller than the current node goes to the:

routineWriter.questionText: Write the recursive insert routine for a BST. The function returns the (possibly new) root.

commonMistakes.description: Base case is NULL root — this is where the new node is created
New leaf has no children — both pointers must be NULL

fullTrace.questionText: Show the BST built by inserting D, A, T, A, S, T, R, U, C, T, U, R, E, S into an initially empty BST (use character values; duplicates are ignored).
fullTrace.note: This is a direct Part-B question from the exam bank. Key result: D is root, A goes left, T goes right. Duplicates (second A, second T, etc.) are skipped. Final unique sequence: D, A, T, S, R, U, C, E.

steps.note: A < D → goes left of D
T > D → goes right of D
S > D, S < T → goes left of T
R > D, R < T, R < S → goes left of S
U > D, U > T → goes right of T
C > A, C < D → goes right of A
E > A, E < D → right of A... E > C → goes right of C

quickfire.question: Searching for a value in a BST that doesn't exist terminates when:

routineWriter.questionText: Write the routine for retrieve (search) in a binary search tree. The bank explicitly names this question: 'Write the routine for retrieve in a binary search tree.' Return the node if found, NULL otherwise.

commonMistakes.description: First base case: reached a dead end — value not in the tree
Second base case: found — return the node, not just 1 or true
Return the recursive result — omitting return discards the found node

quickfire.question: When deleting a BST node that has two children, which node replaces it?
options: The inorder successor (smallest in right subtree)
The inorder predecessor (largest in left subtree) — either works
Both B and C are correct
quickfire.answer: Both B and C are correct

routineWriter.questionText: Write the delete routine for a BST. Handle all three cases: leaf node, one child, two children. Use the inorder successor strategy for the two-children case.

commonMistakes.line: TNode* tmp = root->right; free(root); return tmp;
commonMistakes.description: One-child case: return the surviving child so the parent can relink
Inorder successor is the leftmost node of the right subtree
Copy successor's value up, then delete the successor from the right subtree — do not swap nodes
Must delete the successor from the right subtree after copying its value up
